sources.entry: teebe - Shows every git worktree across your repos, marks which ones a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex) is working in, and live-diffs the files they change.

summary.one_liner: teebe is a native macOS app that shows every git worktree across all your repos in one window, marks which ones a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) is working in, and live-diffs the changed files.
summary.what_it_does: It lists all worktrees of all added repositories in a single list, each with a browsable file tree. Each worktree gets a status mark: agent working, uncommitted changes, commits not yet merged, or merged and safe to delete, and the list can be grouped and sorted by status. It shows when Claude Code or Codex is working or waiting, with optional notifications when a turn finishes, and badges files live as agents or tools edit them. Merge detection accounts for squash merges by checking against default and integration branches, with a background fetch. It can remove one worktree or all safe-to-delete ones after a confirmation, keeping commits only that worktree reached in a hidden backup. It can also create new worktrees on new or existing branches, and shows per-file diffs (unified or side by side) with keyboard shortcuts.
use_cases: monitor several AI coding agents working in parallel
see uncommitted changes across many git worktrees
check which worktrees are merged and safe to delete
clean up stale git worktrees in one step
create new git worktrees without typing git commands
peek at file diffs without opening an IDE
how_to_run: curl -fsSL | bash  (install script; URL missing from README)
Or download teebe.zip / teebe.dmg, unzip, and drag teebe.app into /Applications
Launch from source: swift run Teebe
notable: Merge detection that understands squash merges
Live agent activity for Claude Code and Codex, with optional turn-finished notifications
Keyboard-driven UI with Space to peek diffs and ⌘⇧C to copy files as @-refs for agent prompts
Read-only by design: it watches worktrees and never writes into your repositories
Backs up commits that only a removed worktree still reached
caveats: macOS only, requires macOS 14 or newer, Apple Silicon listed
Not notarized yet, so first launch of a downloaded copy may need manual approval in System Settings
Not a git client, agent runner, or editor: no rebase, cherry-pick, or conflict resolution
